newsitem.title: FINLAND: Big seller seen taking profits in markka debt.
newsitem.headline: Big seller seen taking profits in markka debt.

text.p: A large domestic operator was seen behind heavy selling of markka bonds in early trade on Thursday, catching the rest of the market off-guard and swelling the yield spread over Bunds, analysts said.

The market suddenly weakened after opening a shade stronger on what dealers expected to be just another sleepy summer day, with no response to widely expected confirmation France would miss the deficit target for economic and monetary union (EMU).
The surprise selling of the 7.25 percent 2006 benchmark pushed the yield up two basis points, and with Bunds firming slightly the spread widened to 35 basis points from 30. @
"This is not general sentiment, just few bigger names," said analyst Juha Lehtonen at Merita Bank.
But other analysts speaking on condition of anonymity said one big domestic market operator was behind the move.
By 1135/0835 GMT, the yield on the 2006 bond was 6.00 percent, up from 5.98 percent at Thursday's close. The spread over bunds had retreated one basis point to 34 bps.
The 2006 yield ducked below six percent on Tuesday for the first time since mid-March, which analysts said may have invited selective profit-taking. @
"They played it very skilfully, picking a very good moment to unload bonds," one senior treasury market analyst said.
The timing of the sale was probably more linked to the imminent closing of January-June accounts than to any new view on Finland's economic fundamentals, he added.
Another treasury economist said the sale was unlikely to prompt other major holders of Finnish government paper to follow suit. "Most investors are on the sidelines," he said.
